subject.title: The Skill Accumulation Problem: How many skills before your agent gets confused?

question: Should ClawHub own task-context skill recommendation and conflict/load-policy metadata for accumulated agent skill sets, and where is the boundary between registry metadata and OpenClaw runtime behavior?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow source defect; it defines new product semantics across recommender inputs, publisher metadata, local agent state, privacy, and runtime conflict resolution.

options.title: Keep as product RFC
options.body: Maintain this issue as the canonical discussion until maintainers define the registry/runtime contract and then split implementation work into narrower issues.

options.title: Scope a narrow docs-only follow-up
options.body: Document current best practices for pruning, layering, and pinning without adding recommender or conflict metadata yet.

options.title: Close as covered by current ranking and pinning
options.body: Treat current global recommendation, related browsing, dependency metadata, and pinning as sufficient, leaving task-context and conflict policy out of scope.

recommendation.title: Keep as product RFC
recommendation.body: Maintain this issue as the canonical discussion until maintainers define the registry/runtime contract and then split implementation work into narrower issues.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS routes the central schema, API, and CLI surfaces likely affected by any permanent contract.
